recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Future preferred-contact changes should be driven by a new PA or MnM decision if the work groups want a mechanism beyond Patient.communication.preferred and ContactPoint.rank.
issue_request: FHIR-7086 was a Published FHIR-core Patient change request, resolved Persuasive with Modification, asking whether Patient communication should include a preferred method such as sign language, Braille, email, or telephone. The recorded resolution says ContactPoint had been updated with a rank property that permits ordering contact points by preference.
initial_application: No git commit message was found that explicitly mentions FHIR-7086 or 2015May core #145. The substantive application is the closely related ContactPoint rank work: FHIR-7626 requested a rank attribute for communication modalities, and historical commit d45b815efc6c29cd65295e44bf82863887c82875 added ContactPoint.rank. FHIR-7626 is already represented on the combined branch by commit ced4ab500919bbc63ab62fd9734aca1962b5db9c.
additional_context: Patient is an active resource and ContactPoint is an active normative datatype in source/fhir.ini. Current Patient source defines Patient.telecom as ContactPoint and Patient.communication.preferred as the language preference indicator, with sign-language examples in the language comment. Later final issues FHIR-16984, FHIR-38824, and FHIR-12593 kept and clarified ContactPoint.rank; FHIR-31615 later declined a broader ambiguous preferred-method extension request.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit is needed because the current build-scoped source already expresses both relevant preference mechanisms: Patient.communication.preferred for language preference and ContactPoint.rank for ordered telephone/email/contact-point preference through Patient.telecom.

related_jiras.note: Requested and applied the ContactPoint.rank element that FHIR-7086 cites as its final resolution; already audited on the combined branch.
Clarified that lower ContactPoint.rank values are more preferred and avoided implying array order.
Added current comments that ranks need not be unique or sequential and that unranked repetitions are allowed.
Rejected removal of ContactPoint.rank because explicit rank is needed when repeating-element order is not meaningful.
Later PA no-change decision declined an ambiguous preferred-method extension request and does not require changing Patient for this seed.
